title: 7–18 February – 51st Berlin International Film Festival
text: The 51st annual Berlin International Film Festival was held from February 7 to 18, 2001. The festival opened with war-drama film Enemy at the Gates by Jean-Jacques Annaud.

title: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 2001
text: Germany was represented at the Eurovision Song Contest 2001 with the song "Wer Liebe lebt" written by Gino Trovatello, Matthias Stingl, and Eva Richter, and performed by Michelle. The German participating broadcaster on behalf of ARD, Norddeutscher Rundfunk, organised the national final Countdown Grand Prix Eurovision 2001 in order to select their entry for the contest.
wiki: Germany in the Eurovision Song Contest 2001

title: Baden-Württemberg state election, 2001
text: The 2001 Baden-Württemberg state election was held on 25 March 2001 to elect the members of the 12th Landtag of Baden-Württemberg. The incumbent coalition government of the Christian Democratic Union and Free Democratic Party (FDP) under Minister-President Erwin Teufel was re-elected with an increased majority and continued in office.

title: Rhineland-Palatinate state election, 2001
text: The 2001 Rhineland-Palatinate state election was held on 25 March 2001 to elect the members of the Landtag of Rhineland-Palatinate. The incumbent coalition government of the Social Democratic Party and Free Democratic Party (FDP) led by Minister-President Kurt Beck retained its majority and continued in office.

title: Arena AufSchalke in Gelsenkirchen is opened.
text: Arena AufSchalke, currently known as Veltins-Arena (pronounced ) for sponsorship reasons, is a football stadium with a retractable roof and slide-out pitch in Gelsenkirchen, North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It opened on 13 August 2001 as the new home ground of FC Schalke 04.

title: Hamburg state election, 2001
text: The 2001 Hamburg state election was held on 23 September 2001 to elect the members of the 17th Hamburg Parliament. The incumbent coalition government of the Social Democratic Party and Green Alternative List (GAL) led by First Mayor Ortwin Runde was defeated, ending 44 years of uninterrupted SPD rule in the city-state.

title: Berlin state election, 2001
text: The 2001 Berlin state election was held on 21 October 2001 to elect the members of the 15th Abgeordnetenhaus of Berlin. Prior to the election, Mayor Klaus Wowereit had led a minority government of the Social Democratic Party and The Greens since June, which had replaced a coalition between the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and SPD which collapsed in June.

title: Date unknown – German company ZF Sachs was sold to ZF Friedrichshafen AG, and renamed to ZF Sachs AG.
text: ZF Sachs AG, also known as Fichtel & Sachs, was founded in Schweinfurt in 1895 and was a well-known German family business. At its last point as an independent company, the company name was Fichtel & Sachs AG. In 1997, the automotive supplier was taken over by Mannesmann and renamed Mannesmann Sachs AG. As of 2001, Sachs belonged to ZF Friedrichshafen as a subsidiary company ZF Sachs AG. In 2011, ZF Sachs, like ot…

title: “Es ist geil ein Arschloch zu sein” by Christian
text: "Es ist geil ein Arschloch zu sein" is a song by German singer and Big Brother Germany contestant Christian. Following his brief and controversial tenure on the programme, Christian quit the show and capitalised on his notoriety in Germany to record the track, which was written by Steve van Velvet and produced by Bülent Aris in Hamburg, Germany.

title: “Stan” by 29 January
text: "Stan" is a song by American rapper Eminem, with vocals sampled from the opening lines of English singer Dido's song "Thank You". It was released on November 20, 2000, as the third single from Eminem's third album, The Marshall Mathers LP.

title: “Ms. Jackson” by Outkast
text: "Ms. Jackson" is a song by the American hip-hop duo Outkast, consisting of André 3000 and Big Boi.

title: “Daylight in Your Eyes” by 19 February
text: "Daylight in Your Eyes" is the debut single by German girl group No Angels. It was written by Tony Bruno and Tommy Byrnes and initially recorded by American rock band New Life Crisis.

title: “Butterfly” by 2 April
text: "Butterfly" is a song by American rap rock band Crazy Town. The song was released in October 2000 as the third single from their debut album, The Gift of Game.

title: “Dream On” by 7 May
text: "Dream On" is a song by English electronic music band Depeche Mode. It was released in the United States on 17 April 2001 and in the United Kingdom on 23 April 2001 as the first single from the band's tenth studio album, Exciter.

title: “Whole Again” by 21 May
text: "Whole Again" is a song by the English girl group Atomic Kitten for their debut studio album, Right Now. The original demo, first included on the Japanese release, was co-written and produced by Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark members and Atomic Kitten founders Andy McCluskey and Stuart Kershaw under their production moniker Engine, with Jem Godfrey and Bill Padley providing additional songwriting and production…

title: “Miss California” by Dante Thomas
text: "Miss California" is a song by American singer Dante Thomas, featuring American rapper and former Fugees member Pras Michel. It was released on February 20, 2001, as the lead single from his debut album, Fly.

title: “Lady Marmalade” by Christina Aguilera, Pink, Lil' Kim and Mýa featuring Missy Elliott
text: "Lady Marmalade" is a song written by Bob Crewe and Kenny Nolan and popularized in 1974 by the American funk rock group Labelle. It is best known for its French refrain of "Voulez-vous coucher avec moi, ce soir?", a sexual proposition that translates into English as "Do you want to come to bed with me, tonight?" Released as a single on November 5, 1974, Labelle's version held the number-one spot on the Billboard H…

title: “Angel” by Shaggy featuring Rayvon
text: "Angel" is a song by Jamaican reggae artist Shaggy featuring Barbadian singer Rayvon. It is the second single from Shaggy's fifth studio album, Hot Shot.

title: “Follow Me” by Uncle Kracker
text: "Follow Me" is a song by American musician Uncle Kracker. It was released as his debut solo single on November 6, 2000, serving as lead single from his first studio album, Double Wide.

title: “There Must Be an Angel” by 27 August
text: "There Must Be an Angel" is a song by the British musical duo Eurythmics, released as the second single from their fifth studio album, Be Yourself Tonight (1985). It features a harmonica solo by American musician Stevie Wonder.
wiki: There Must Be an Angel (Playing with My Heart)
listen: There Must Be an Angel 27 August

title: “Only Time” by 1 October
text: "Only Time" is a song by Irish musician Enya. It was released on 6 November 2000 as the lead single from her fifth studio album, A Day Without Rain.

title: “Can't Get You Out of My Head” by Kylie Minogue
text: "Can't Get You Out of My Head" is a song recorded by Australian singer Kylie Minogue for her eighth studio album, Fever. Parlophone Records released the song as the album's lead single on 8 September 2001.
wiki: Can't Get You Out of My Head
listen: Can't Get You Out of My Head Kylie Minogue

title: “Because I Got High” by Afroman
text: "Because I Got High" is a comedy hip-hop song by American rapper Afroman from the 2000 album of the same name and released as a single the following year. The lyrics of the song humorously describe how cannabis use is degrading the narrator's quality of life.

title: “From Sarah with Love” by Sarah Connor
text: "From Sarah with Love" is a song by German recording artist Sarah Connor. It was co-written and produced by Rob Tyger and Kay Denar and Connor for her debut studio album, Green Eyed Soul.
listen: From Sarah with Love Sarah Connor

title: “I Believe” by 17 December
text: "I Believe" is a song by German pop group Bro'Sis. It was written by Alex Christensen, Jens Klein, Peter Könemann, and Clyde "J. Ena" "Ward and produced by the former for their debut studio album, Never Forget (2001).

title: The NEAR Shoemaker spacecraft lands in the "saddle" region of 433 Eros, becoming the first spacecraft to land on an asteroid.
text: Near Earth Asteroid Rendezvous, later renamed NEAR Shoemaker in honor of planetary scientist Eugene Shoemaker, was a robotic space probe developed by the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory for NASA. Launched in 1996, it was designed to study the near-Earth asteroid 433 Eros from orbit over the course of a year. It was the first spacecraft to orbit an asteroid and successfully land on one.

title: NASA's Genesis spacecraft is launched.
text: Genesis was a NASA sample-return probe that collected a sample of solar wind particles and returned them to Earth for analysis. It was the first NASA sample-return mission to return material since the Apollo program, and the first to return material from beyond the orbit of the Moon.

title: NASA's Galileo spacecraft passes within 112 miles (180 km) of Jupiter's moon Io.
text: Galileo was an American robotic space probe that studied the planet Jupiter and its moons, as well as the asteroids Gaspra and Ida. Named after the Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei, it consisted of an orbiter and an entry probe.

title: The Hubble Space Telescope detects sodium in the atmosphere of HD 209458 b, the first exoplanet atmosphere to be measured.
text: The Hubble Space Telescope is a space telescope that was launched into low Earth orbit in 1990 and remains in operation. It was not the first space telescope, but it is one of the largest and most versatile, renowned as a vital research tool and as a public relations boon for astronomy.

title: The author Michael Crichton signs a new deal with HarperCollins Publishers that reportedly earns him $40 million for two books.
text: John Michael Crichton was an American author and filmmaker. His books have sold over 200 million copies worldwide, and over a dozen have been adapted into films.

title: The BookCrossing scheme for leaving books for strangers to find is launched.
text: BookCrossing is defined as the practice of leaving a book in a public place to be 'caught' by others, who may then do likewise. The term is derived from bookcrossing.com, a free online book community which was founded in 2001 to encourage the practice, aiming to "make the whole world a library." The "crossing" or exchanging of books may take any of a number of forms, including the 'wild-release' of a book in publi…

title: The film version of Helen Fielding's 1996 novel Bridget Jones's Diary has uncredited cameo roles as themselves for Salman Rushdie, Julian Barnes and Jeffrey Archer, at a literary party.
text: Helen Fielding is a British journalist, novelist and screenwriter, best known as the creator of the fictional character Bridget Jones. Fielding’s first novel was set in a refugee camp in East Africa and she started writing Bridget Jones in an anonymous column in London’s Independent newspaper.

title: The English popular novelist and politician Jeffrey Archer, having been found guilty of perjury in a libel trial, is sentenced to imprisonment.
text: Jeffrey Howard Archer, Baron Archer of Weston-super-Mare, was an English novelist, politician and convicted criminal. He was the Member of Parliament (MP) for Louth (Lincolnshire) from 1969 to 1974, but did not seek re-election after almost going bankrupt.

title: Amiri Baraka reads his poem "Somebody Blew Up America?" at a poetry festival in New Jersey, eight days after the September 11 attacks.
text: Amiri Baraka, previously known as LeRoi Jones and Imamu Amear Baraka, was an American writer of poetry, drama, fiction, essays, and music criticism. He was the author of numerous books of poetry and taught at several universities, including the University at Buffalo and Stony Brook University.

title: Film premiere of Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone, first in the commercially successful Harry Potter film series based on the novels of J. K. Rowling.
text: Joanne Rowling, better known by her pen name J. K. Rowling, is a British author, philanthropist, producer, and screenwriter. She is best known for writing Harry Potter, a seven-volume series about a young wizard and the best-selling book series in history, with over 600 million copies sold.

title: The live-action film version of J. R. R. Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring, directed by Peter Jackson, opens in London. Its appearance has a strong impact on readership of the trilogy.
text: John Ronald Reuel Tolkien was an English writer and academic philologist. He was the author of the high fantasy works The Hobbit (1937) and The Lord of the Rings (1954–1955).

title: A black monolith measuring approximately 9 feet tall appears in Seattle, Washington's Magnuson Park, placed by an anonymous artist in reference to the movie 2001: A Space Odyssey.
text: In Arthur C. Clarke's Space Odyssey series, Monoliths are machines in black cuboids whose sides extend in the precise ratio of 1 : 4 : 9 built by an unseen extraterrestrial species whom Clarke dubbed the Firstborn and who he suggests are the earliest highly intelligent species to evolve in the Milky Way. In the series of novels (and the films based on these), three Monoliths are discovered in the Solar System by a…

title: Unveiling of Rachel Whiteread's Untitled Monument on the Fourth plinth, Trafalgar Square, London.
text: Dame Rachel Whiteread is an English artist who primarily produces sculptures, which typically take the form of casts. She was the first woman to win the annual Turner Prize in 1993.

title: Inauguration of the Altamira cave replica created by Manuel Franquelo and Sven Nebel.
text: The Cave of Altamira is a cave complex, located near the historic town of Santillana del Mar in Cantabria, Spain. It is renowned for prehistoric cave art featuring charcoal drawings and polychrome paintings of contemporary local fauna and human hands.

title: An estimated $100 million worth of art is destroyed in the 11 September attacks on New York City. Public artwork accounts for around $10 million of this figure, which includes works by Alexander Calder, Joan Miró and Roy Lichtenstein.
text: The September 11 attacks, colloquially known as 9/11, were a coordinated series of suicide attacks perpetrated by the Islamic terrorist organization al-Qaeda against the United States in 2001. A total of 19 hijackers commandeered four commercial passenger airliners.

title: Fritz Koenig's Great Spherical Caryatid ("The Sphere") is the only surviving artwork following the September 11 attacks. It is repurposed as a memorial.
text: Fritz Koenig was a German sculptor, considered one of the most important international German sculptors of the 20th century. Koenig's main work and most famous work is The Sphere.
